novel_features.name: Unsubscribe compliance check
novel_features.description: See which senders kept mailing you after a one-click unsubscribe, with an escalation query per violator.
novel_features.rationale: Requires joining the local unsubscribe ledger against post-unsubscribe arrivals in the synced store — one-click is fire-and-forget in every other tool.
novel_features.why_it_matters: After running unsubscribes, this is the only way to learn which ones actually stuck before escalating to block/filter decisions.

novel_features.name: Mailbox delta report
novel_features.description: Everything new since your last check: new messages per category and sender, never-seen senders, volume spikes.
novel_features.rationale: Requires a local checkpoint row plus synced tables — a live API can only re-list, it cannot diff against what was already reported.
novel_features.why_it_matters: The first question of any recurring mailbox check is what changed — this answers it without re-reporting what the operator already saw.

novel_features.name: Storage attribution report
novel_features.description: Which senders, labels, years, and attachments own your storage, with ready-to-run cleanup queries per row.
novel_features.rationale: Gmail exposes only a profile total; attribution requires local aggregation over sizeEstimate, labels, and dates.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Turns a vague quota number into a ranked hit-list whose rows paste straight into cleanup plan.

novel_features.name: Saved cleanup rules
novel_features.description: Named local recipes (query plus trash or label action) replayed through the preview-confirm-undo engine as one merged plan.
novel_features.rationale: Server-side Gmail filters are structurally absent from this binary; a local rulebook replayed through the safe engine is the compliant recurrence path.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Standing hygiene (old promos to trash, receipts to their folder) becomes one command a scheduled job can run daily, always previewed before applying.

novel_features.name: Sort suggestions
novel_features.description: Senders whose mail you already label consistently, with a generated plan to label the rest the same way.
novel_features.rationale: Requires majority-label statistics over messages, labels, and senders in the local store — mechanical, LLM-free categorization.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Folder-sorting at scale without guessing: the plan only proposes what the operator's own labeling history already proves.

novel_features.name: Trash undo-window watch
novel_features.description: What you trashed, grouped by applied plan, with days remaining before Gmail's 30-day purge makes undo impossible.
novel_features.rationale: Requires the local mutation ledger joined to trash state — the API has no memory of why or when something was trashed.
novel_features.why_it_matters: The last regret-check: surfaces batches whose undo window is closing so recovery happens while it still can.

novel_features.name: Mailbox health score
novel_features.description: Per-account hygiene metrics — unread share, promo share, subscription count, storage headroom — snapshotted over time.
novel_features.rationale: Requires local aggregates persisted to a snapshots table; week-over-week campaign progress no single API call can report.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Shows whether the cleanup campaign is actually winning — Promotions down 60% since baseline beats a feeling.

narrative.headline: Mailbox cleanup that can prove itself — preview, confirm, undo, verify — from a binary that structurally cannot send email.
narrative.value_prop: Every read and cleanup surface from the Gmail tool landscape, multi-account, with a local SQLite store underneath: sender intelligence, all-category digests, bulk trash/label with preview-confirm-undo, RFC 8058 one-click unsubscribes with a compliance ledger. Send, drafts, settings, and permanent deletion are absent from the binary by construction — Trash is the ceiling.
narrative.auth_narrative: Installed-app OAuth with named multi-account profiles (per-profile token store, consented-account verification). The only scope ever requested is gmail.modify; send/draft/settings endpoints do not exist in this binary, and permanent deletion is impossible under this scope — Google enforces the Trash ceiling, not us.

quickstart.comment: One-time OAuth consent per named account profile
Build the local store the intelligence commands run on
The all-category summary: counts, unread aging, top senders per tab
Who actually fills this mailbox — volume, size, unread rate

quickstart.command: gmail-pp-cli cleanup plan --q "category:promotions older_than:1y" --action trash --account personal
quickstart.comment: Preview first, always: counts and samples before anything moves

troubleshoots.fix: Re-run gmail-pp-cli accounts auth --account <name> — the refresh token was revoked (password changes revoke Gmail tokens)

troubleshoots.symptom: sync reports an expired history cursor (HTTP 404)
troubleshoots.fix: Run gmail-pp-cli sync --account <name> --full — Gmail expires historyId cursors after long gaps; a full resync rebuilds cleanly

troubleshoots.symptom: cleanup apply refuses without a plan token
troubleshoots.fix: Run cleanup plan first and pass its printed token to apply — applies never run unplanned
That sender only offers mailto: unsubscribe — it appears in unsub audit --mailto-only for manual handling; this tool never sends email

narrative.when_to_use: Reach for this CLI when an agent or operator needs to understand or clean a Gmail mailbox safely: summaries across every category, sender and storage intelligence, bulk trash/label with preview and undo, and one-click unsubscribes with follow-up verification. It is the wrong tool for composing or sending anything — by design it cannot.
